first.rationale: Targeted promotional pricing most directly addresses the immediate loss of price-sensitive SMB accounts and has inherited evidence of acquisition and revenue lift. However, its effect on sustainable qualified revenue, retention, and post-promotion economics is not established, so memory_73 should be verified. Memory_86 should also be checked because onboarding deterioration creates a credible lower-risk alternative, but its evidence currently stops at early adoption rather than long-term revenue. Pending verification, use a guarded, tightly targeted test rather than a broad discount.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source shows higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding decline while supporting sustainable revenue. Reject promotional pricing despite its acquisition lift because verified retention fell 12% and the cohort did not survive first renewal. Long-term qualified-revenue impact from onboarding remains indirect, so retain an experimental holdout and measure activation, qualified conversion, retention, and expansion.
